title: [CRY2-4] SFrame KID layout can make two senders share a KID, which reuses nonces under the shared `
description: Review finding CRY2-4: SFrame KID layout can make two senders share a KID, which reuses nonces under the shared `base_key` (lens CRY2). Location: spec/06-calls.md:222, 479. Fix: Confirmed against RFC 9605 §5.2 (rfc9605.txt:866-867): "Let S be the number of bits required to encode a member index in the group, i.e., the smallest value such that group_size <= (1 << S)." The RFC is itself ambiguous about "group_size". Counterexample: members sit at leaves 0, 1 and 5, so the member count is 3 and S = 2. KID(context 0, index 5) = 0x50+e equals KID(context 1, index 1) = 0x40+0x10+e, which reuses (key, nonce). Correct the citation: the leaf count is defined in RFC 9420 §4.1 ("The _size_ of a tree ... is the number of leaf nodes it contains"; every tree is perfect, with 2^d leaves), not §7.1, which covers ParentNode contents. Fix at 06:222: "S is the depth of the epoch's ratchet tree, that is, the smallest value with (number of leaves, including blank leaves, RFC 9420 §4.1) <= (1 << S)". 06:479 inherits the fix. Add a test vector with blank leaves. Full text: notes/review2/CRY2-verified.md and notes/review2/CRY2.md.
